| N-1 | defect | MINOR | The recovery notice — the behaviour added specifically to close R-03 — has no test. CLAIM: `notifyRecovered` and the `if (publication.noticeShown) publication.notifyRecovered()` branch are never executed by any test in the suite; the string `set after retry` appears in no test file. PROOF: the one test that drives the reassert path, index.test.ts:271 'reasserts immediately on the first turn when startup publication missed', fires turn_start while the primary window is still SLEEPING at its 250ms step, so `noticeShown` is false when the reassert resolves and the recovery branch is skipped — the test then asserts only the ABSENCE of the failure notice. The branch is reachable in production (primary exhausts at 10s and notices, first turn arrives after that, reassert succeeds), which is precisely the standing-false-warning case R-03 reported. So the fix for a reported finding is itself in the state that finding's parent, R-01, was raised for. Severity is MINOR rather than MAJOR because the untested surface is one info-level notice, not the publication or cancellation logic R-01 covered. SMALLEST FIX: extend the existing test — construct it with a short schedule so the primary exhausts and notices BEFORE turn_start fires, then assert both `could not set omp session name` and `omp session name set after retry — id is &lt;self&gt;` are present, in that order. | .pi/extensions/pij/index.ts:206-209 (notifyRecovered) and :534-537 (the noticeShown branch) | — | — | — | — | — | — |
| N-2 | defect | NIT | The healthy-skip gate reads `!publication.took`, and `took` is only written when the PRIMARY publishSeatName promise resolves. A first turn arriving while the primary is mid-window but destined to succeed therefore still reasserts. This is not a defect against the contract — G1 explicitly licenses one extra attempt on the first user turn, and the extra set is idempotent — but the test that guards it, 'does not reassert on the first turn after startup publication took', proves the skip only for an ALREADY-SETTLED publication: its fake takes on attempt 1, so `await new Promise(setTimeout(0))` is enough for the `.then` to land before turn_start. Name the test after the wire fact it actually establishes ('after the startup publication has RESOLVED as taken'), or add the in-flight case so the gap is a decision rather than an accident. | .pi/extensions/pij/index.ts:526 and index.test.ts:256 | — | — | — | — | — | — |

Unreachable in production now that risk r1 is recorded RESOLVED, so this is a tidiness point only. | N-5 | defect | NIT | `let publication: NonNullable&lt;typeof ompSessionNamePublication&gt;;` is declared uninitialised and then captured by the `notice` and `notifyRecovered` closures, which dereference `publication.noticeShown` before the declaration is assigned at :197. | V2-R01 | N-1 | fixed | R-01 (MAJOR) CLOSED. Three wiring tests now exist and I ran them: index.test.ts:256 healthy-no-reassert, :271 first-turn-miss-reasserts, :290 shutdown-cancels-the-stale-window. I judged each non-vacuous by inspection rather than by mutation, per the ruling: delete the `!publication.took` gate and :256 goes red (two names instead of one); delete the turn_start reassert and :271 goes red (it asserts length 2 SYNCHRONOUSLY after turn_start, which only the immediate reassert can satisfy — the primary's own next attempt is 250ms away); delete the generation guard in the `setSessionName` dep and :290 goes red (the sleeping window would push a second name at 250ms). All three therefore witness the guards they name. Residue, tracked as N-1: the recovery-notice branch added in the same change is not among them. Partial-coverage note, not a finding: :290 proves cancellation on SHUTDOWN only — the execution log's broader claim, that a stale generation cannot overwrite a REPLACEMENT session, still has no test for the reload path that mints a successor. | — | — | — | — |
| V2-R02 | N-4 | refuted | R-02 CLOSED, downgraded MAJOR -&gt; MINOR in the r1 addendum and now discharged. The control run refuted the load-bearing half — the `--no-extensions -e` shape still races against the pre-fix extension (1 miss in 10, pij-pretty-fly) — so the objection that the launch shape had removed the variable under test is dead. AC1's note has been rewritten to cite the control, which is the right disposition. I stand by the arithmetic on the record: at the 10% pre-fix rate observed AT THIS SHAPE, 10/10 is p=0.35 and does not separate the retry from luck at n=10; what the control proves DETERMINISTICALLY is G2's — the pre-fix miss capture has no fallback row at all, while every branch witness carries the keyed row by construction. The AC is true; its strength lives in the second surface, not the count. | — | — | — | — |
| V2-R03 | N-1 | fixed | R-03 CLOSED on the mechanism, with its own fix untested (N-1). The reassert now fires IMMEDIATELY at turn_start instead of chaining onto the settled primary promise, so an early first turn can land the name before the 10s window expires and no false warning is ever printed — the common case is now correct by construction rather than by luck. For the late-turn case the warning still prints first, but `notifyRecovered` follows it with `pij: omp session name set after retry — id is &lt;self&gt;` at info level, gated on `noticeShown` so a session that never warned gets no spurious recovery line. That is a better answer than the one I proposed (suppressing the notice until after the reassert), because it keeps G3's 'never silence' promise intact while retracting the claim honestly. It also resolves the interface drift I raised in the r1 addendum: `took` is retained on the publication and the gate is back, so u1's 'if it had not taken' holds again. | — | — | — | — |
